title: Base change preserves flatness at a module point
statement: Let A, B, R and S be commutative rings in a commuting square A -> B, R -> S with maps A -> R and B -> S. Suppose the square is a tensor-product pushout. Let N be a B-module, regarded as an A-module, and let M be an S-module, regarded as an R-module. Suppose e: S tensor_B N -> M is an S-linear isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For a prime q of S put p = q intersect B [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If N_p is flat over A [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then M_q is flat over R. No finiteness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Theorem Tag 00RC, reduction paragraph, lines 33446-33457; Lemma Tag 00HI; Lemma Tag 00HT, proof of (6)-(7)

proof.text: Let p be the contraction of q. Flat base change makes R tensor_A N_p flat over R. The pushout cancellation equivalence Algebra.IsPushout.cancelBaseChange identifies it with S tensor_B N_p. The latter is therefore R-flat.

Tensor N -> N_p with S. By tensor symmetry and IsLocalizedModule.rTensor this map is a localization at the image in S of the complement of p. Precompose with e inverse to obtain a localization map f from M to P = S tensor_B N_p.

For an ideal J of R and y in the kernel of M tensor_R J -> M tensor_R R, naturality of tensor maps shows that (f tensor J)(y) maps to zero under P tensor_R J -> P tensor_R R. Flatness of P makes this map injective, so (f tensor J)(y)=0. Tensor-localization compatibility and its zero criterion give a denominator in the image of B minus p annihilating y.

Every such denominator is outside q, by contraction. The localized tensor-kernel criterion Module.flat_localizedModule_iff proves the conclusion. Its criterion is the zero criterion for module localization applied to tensor maps; all of this glue is explicitly proved in the delivered Lean.
